===== node_modules\vite\README.md =====

# Vite ⚡

> Next Generation Frontend Tooling

- 💡 Instant Server Start
- ⚡️ Lightning Fast HMR
- 🛠️ Rich Features
- 📦 Optimized Build
- 🔩 Universal Plugin Interface
- 🔑 Fully Typed APIs

Vite (French word for "quick", pronounced [`/viːt/`](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/vitejs/vite@main/docs/public/vite.mp3), like "veet") is a build tool that aims to provide a faster and leaner development experience for modern web projects. It consists of two major parts:

- A dev server that provides [rich feature enhancements](https://vite.dev/guide/features) over [native ES modules](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Modules), for example extremely fast [Hot Module Replacement (HMR)](https://vite.dev/guide/features#hot-module-replacement).

- A build command that bundles your code with [Rolldown](https://rolldown.rs), pre-configured to output highly optimized static assets for production.

In addition, Vite is highly extensible via its [Plugin API](https://vite.dev/guide/api-plugin.html) and [JavaScript API](https://vite.dev/guide/api-javascript.html) with full typing support.

[Read the Docs to Learn More](https://vite.dev).


===== node_modules\vitest\node_modules\magic-string\README.md =====

# magic-string

<a href="https://npmjs.org/package/magic-string">
  <img src="https://img.shields.io/npm/v/magic-string.svg"
       alt="npm version">
</a>
<a href="https://github.com/Rich-Harris/magic-string/blob/master/LICENSE.md">
  <img src="https://img.shields.io/npm/l/magic-string.svg"
       alt="license">
</a>

Suppose you have some source code. You want to make some light modifications to it - replacing a few characters here and there, wrapping it with a header and footer, etc - and ideally you'd like to generate a [source map](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1U1RGAehQwRypUTovF1KRlpiOFze0b-_2gc6fAH0KY0k/) at the end of it. You've thought about using something like [recast](https://github.com/benjamn/recast) (which allows you to generate an AST from some JavaScript, manipulate it, and reprint it with a sourcemap without losing your comments and formatting), but it seems like overkill for your needs (or maybe the source code isn't JavaScript).

Your requirements are, frankly, rather niche. But they're requirements that I also have, and for which I made magic-string. It's a small, fast utility for manipulating strings and generating sourcemaps.

## Installation

magic-string works in both node.js and browser environments. For node, install with npm:

```bash
npm i magic-string
```

magic-string is ESM-only. In browsers, import it from an ESM CDN:

```html
<script type="module">
	import MagicString from 'https://unpkg.com/magic-string/dist/index.mjs';
</script>
```

## Usage

These examples assume you're in node.js, or something similar:

```js
import fs from 'node:fs'
import MagicString from 'magic-string'

const s = new MagicString('problems = 99')

s.update(0, 8, 'answer')
s.toString() // 'answer = 99'

s.update(11, 13, '42') // character indices always refer to the original string
s.toString() // 'answer = 42'

s.prepend('var ').append(';') // most methods are chainable
s.toString() // 'var answer = 42;'

const map = s.generateMap({
  source: 'source.js',
  file: 'converted.js.map',
  includeContent: true,
}) // generates a v3 sourcemap

fs.writeFileSync('converted.js', s.toString())
fs.writeFileSync('converted.js.map', map.toString())
```

You can pass an options argument:

```js
const s = new MagicString(someCode, {
  // these options will be used if you later call `bundle.addSource( s )` - see below
  filename: 'foo.js',
  indentExclusionRanges: [
    /* ... */
  ],
  // mark source as ignore in DevTools, see below #Bundling
  ignoreList: false,
  // adjust the incoming position - see below
  offset: 0,
})
```

## Properties

### s.offset

Sets the offset property to adjust the incoming position for the following APIs: `slice`, `update`, `overwrite`, `appendLeft`, `prependLeft`, `appendRight`, `prependRight`, `move`, `reset`, and `remove`.

Example usage:

```ts
const s = new MagicString('hello world', { offset: 0 })
s.offset = 6
s.slice() === 'world'
```

## Hi-res mappings

The `hires` option (passed to `generateMap`/`generateDecodedMap`) controls how granular sourcemap mappings are:

- `false` (default) - lo-res mappings. Only one mapping per line, plus any locations added with `s.addSourcemapLocation()`. Quicker to generate and less bulky, but devtools may only be able to identify the correct line, not the exact column.
- `true` - hi-res mappings. Every single character gets a mapping, so devtools can always pinpoint the exact location of function calls and so on.
- `"boundary"` - semi-hi-res mappings, segmented per word boundary instead of per character. Suitable for string semantics that are separated by words.
- `"experimental-range"` - hi-res mappings that use [range mappings](https://github.com/tc39/ecma426/blob/main/proposals/range-mappings.md), a source map extension that can map all positions in a range with fewer mappings than mapping every character individually. This requires support for range mappings in the source map consumer, and the feature is experimental.

## Methods

### s.addSourcemapLocation( index )

Adds the specified character index (with respect to the original string) to sourcemap mappings, if `hires` is `false` (see [Hi-res mappings](#hi-res-mappings)).

### s.append( content )

Appends the specified content to the end of the string. Returns `this`.

### s.appendLeft( index, content )

Appends the specified `content` at the `index` in the original string. If a range _ending_ with `index` is subsequently moved, the insert will be moved with it. Returns `this`. See also `s.prependLeft(...)`.

### s.appendRight( index, content )

Appends the specified `content` at the `index` in the original string. If a range _starting_ with `index` is subsequently moved, the insert will be moved with it. Returns `this`. See also `s.prependRight(...)`.

### s.clone()

Does what you'd expect.

### s.generateDecodedMap( options )

Generates a sourcemap object with raw mappings in array form, rather than encoded as a string. See `generateMap` documentation below for options details. Useful if you need to manipulate the sourcemap further, but most of the time you will use `generateMap` instead.

### s.generateMap( options )

Generates a [version 3 sourcemap](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1U1RGAehQwRypUTovF1KRlpiOFze0b-_2gc6fAH0KY0k/edit). All options are, well, optional:

- `file` - the filename where you plan to write the sourcemap
- `source` - the filename of the file containing the original source
- `includeContent` - whether to include the original content in the map's `sourcesContent` array
- `hires` - whether the mapping should be high-resolution. See [Hi-res mappings](#hi-res-mappings) for the available modes. If sourcemap locations have been specified with `s.addSourcemapLocation()`, they will be used here.

The returned sourcemap has two (non-enumerable) methods attached for convenience:

- `toString` - returns the equivalent of `JSON.stringify(map)`
- `toUrl` - returns a DataURI containing the sourcemap. Useful for doing this sort of thing:

```js
code += `\n//# sourceMappingURL=${map.toUrl()}`
```

### s.getIndentString()

Returns the indentation string guessed from the original content, falling back to a single tab character. This is the value `s.indent()` uses when no prefix is supplied.

### s.hasChanged()

Indicates if the string has been changed.

### s.indent( prefix[, options] )

Prefixes each line of the string with `prefix`. If `prefix` is not supplied, the indentation will be guessed from the original content, falling back to a single tab character. Returns `this`.

Lines are counted in the generated string, so content added with `append*`/`prepend*` is indented too, and a line break inside that content starts a new line just like a line break in the original:

```js
const s = new MagicString('var a = 1;\nvar b = 2;')

s.prependRight(11, 'debugger;\n')
s.toString() // 'var a = 1;\ndebugger;\nvar b = 2;'

s.indent('  ')
s.toString() // '  var a = 1;\n  debugger;\n  var b = 2;'
```

The `options` argument can have an `exclude` property, which is an array of `[start, end]` character ranges. These ranges will be excluded from the indentation - useful for (e.g.) multiline strings.

### s.isEmpty()

Returns true if the resulting source is empty (disregarding white space).

### s.lastChar()

Returns the last character of the generated string, or `''` if it is empty.

### s.lastLine()

Returns everything after the last newline in the generated string, or the whole string if there is no newline.

### s.length()

Returns the length of the generated string, counting only content attached to the original characters. Content that sits outside the string body is not counted, so `s.length()` and `s.toString().length` can disagree:

```js
const s = new MagicString('abcde')

s.appendLeft(2, '__')
s.toString() // 'ab__cde'
s.length() // 7

s.prepend('>>')
s.toString() // '>>ab__cde'
s.length() // still 7
```

`s.prepend()` and `s.append()` always land outside the body, as do inserts made before the first character or after the last one.

### s.move( start, end, index[, affinity] )

Moves the characters from `start` and `end` to `index`. Returns `this`.

`affinity` (`'left'` or `'right'`, defaulting to `'right'`) controls where the range is anchored at `index`: `'right'` inserts it before the content that starts at `index`, `'left'` inserts it after the content that ends at `index`. The two differ only when other content has already been moved to that boundary, mirroring the `appendLeft`/`appendRight` distinction.

### s.overwrite( start, end, content[, options] )

Replaces the characters from `start` to `end` with `content`, along with the appended/prepended content in that range. The same restrictions as `s.remove()` apply. Returns `this`.

The fourth argument is optional. It can have a `storeName` property — if `true`, the original name will be stored for later inclusion in a sourcemap's `names` array — and a `contentOnly` property which determines whether only the content is overwritten, or anything that was appended/prepended to the range as well.

It may be preferred to use `s.update(...)` instead if you wish to avoid overwriting the appended/prepended content.

> [!NOTE]
> `overwrite`/`update`/`remove` operate on ranges of the **original** string, so they'll throw (e.g. `cannot overwrite across a split point`, `cannot split a chunk that has already been edited`) when an edit would split a chunk that was previously replaced with non-empty content, or when a replacement crosses moved chunks. If you run into this, or want to chain multiple rounds of edits on a single instance with an auto-combined sourcemap, see [magic-string-stack](https://github.com/antfu/magic-string-stack).

### s.prepend( content )

Prepends the string with the specified content. Returns `this`.

### s.prependLeft ( index, content )

Same as `s.appendLeft(...)`, except that the inserted content will go _before_ any previous appends or prepends at `index`

### s.prependRight ( index, content )

Same as `s.appendRight(...)`, except that the inserted content will go _before_ any previous appends or prepends at `index`

### s.replace( regexpOrString, substitution )

String replacement with RegExp or string. The `substitution` parameter supports strings and functions. Returns `this`.

```ts
import MagicString from 'magic-string'

const s = new MagicString(source)

s.replace('foo', 'bar')
s.replace('foo', (str, index, s) => `${str}-${index}`)
s.replace(/foo/g, 'bar')
s.replace(/(\w)(\d+)/g, (_, $1, $2) => $1.toUpperCase() + $2)
```

The differences from [`String.replace`](<(https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/String/replace)>):

- It will always match against the **original string**
- It mutates the magic string state (use `.clone()` to be immutable)
- A zero-length match spans no characters, so there is nothing to overwrite - the
  substitution is inserted at the matched position, as if by `s.appendRight(index, substitution)`

### s.replaceAll( regexpOrString, substitution )

Same as `s.replace`, but replace all matched strings instead of just one.
If `regexpOrString` is a regex, then it must have the global (`g`) flag set, or a `TypeError` is thrown. Matches the behavior of the builtin [`String.property.replaceAll`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/String/replaceAll). Returns `this`.

### s.remove( start, end )

Removes the characters from `start` to `end` (of the original string, **not** the generated string). Content appended or prepended at positions strictly inside the range is removed along with it, while content attached at `start` or `end` is preserved — use `s.overwrite( start, end, '' )` to remove the range including its edge inserts. Repeated removals and removals with partially overlapping ranges are allowed. Returns `this`.

### s.reset( start, end )

Resets the characters from `start` to `end` (of the original string, **not** the generated string).
It can be used to restore previously removed characters and discard unwanted changes.

### s.slice( start, end )

Returns the content of the generated string that corresponds to the slice between `start` and `end` of the original string. Throws error if the indices are for characters that were already removed.

### s.snip( start, end )

Returns a clone of `s`, with all content before the `start` and `end` characters of the original string removed.

### s.toString()

Returns the generated string.

### s.trim([ charType ])

Trims content matching `charType` (defaults to `\s`, i.e. whitespace) from the start and end. Returns `this`.

### s.trimStart([ charType ])

Trims content matching `charType` (defaults to `\s`, i.e. whitespace) from the start. Returns `this`.

### s.trimEnd([ charType ])

Trims content matching `charType` (defaults to `\s`, i.e. whitespace) from the end. Returns `this`.

### s.trimLines()

Removes empty lines from the start and end. Returns `this`.

### s.update( start, end, content[, options] )

Replaces the characters from `start` to `end` with `content`. The same restrictions as `s.remove()` apply. Returns `this`.

The fourth argument is optional. It can have a `storeName` property — if `true`, the original name will be stored for later inclusion in a sourcemap's `names` array — and an `overwrite` property which defaults to `false` and determines whether anything that was appended/prepended to the range will be overwritten along with the original content.

Without `overwrite`, all of that content is kept, no matter how earlier edits have split the range: content attached at `start` stays in front of the new content, and the rest follows it in its original order.

`s.update(start, end, content)` is equivalent to `s.overwrite(start, end, content, { contentOnly: true })`.

## Bundling

To concatenate several sources, use `Bundle`:

```js
import MagicString, { Bundle } from 'magic-string'

const bundle = new Bundle()

bundle.addSource({
  filename: 'foo.js',
  content: new MagicString('var answer = 42;'),
})

bundle.addSource({
  filename: 'bar.js',
  content: new MagicString('console.log( answer )'),
})

// Sources can be marked as ignore-listed, which provides a hint to debuggers
// to not step into this code and also don't show the source files depending
// on user preferences.
bundle.addSource({
  filename: 'some-3rdparty-library.js',
  content: new MagicString('function myLib(){}'),
  ignoreList: false, // <--
})

// Advanced: a source can include an `indentExclusionRanges` property
// alongside `filename` and `content`. This will be passed to `s.indent()`
// - see documentation above

bundle
  .indent() // optionally, pass an indent string, otherwise it will be guessed
  .prepend('(function () {\n')
  .append('}());')

bundle.toString()
// (function () {
//   var answer = 42;
//   console.log( answer );
// }());

// options are as per `s.generateMap()` above
const map = bundle.generateMap({
  file: 'bundle.js',
  includeContent: true,
  hires: true,
})
```

`includeContent` can also be a function that receives `{ filename, content }` for each source and returns whether to include it, allowing per-source control:

```js
bundle.generateMap({
  includeContent: source => !source.filename.startsWith('http'),
})
```

As an alternative syntax, if you a) don't have `filename` or `indentExclusionRanges` options, or b) passed those in when you used `new MagicString(...)`, you can simply pass the `MagicString` instance itself:

```js
const bundle = new Bundle()
const source = new MagicString(someCode, {
  filename: 'foo.js',
})

bundle.addSource(source)
```

### new Bundle([ options ])

The constructor takes an optional options object:

- `intro` (default `''`) is placed at the start of the bundle, before the first source.
- `separator` (default `'\n'`) is placed between sources.

```js
const bundle = new Bundle({
  intro: '/* my-bundle.js */\n',
  separator: '\n\n',
})

bundle.addSource(new MagicString('var answer = 42;'))
bundle.addSource(new MagicString('console.log(answer);'))

bundle.toString()
// /* my-bundle.js */
// var answer = 42;
//
// console.log(answer);
```

A source can override the bundle separator with its own `separator` property:

```js
const bundle = new Bundle({ separator: '\n\n' })

bundle.addSource(new MagicString('var answer = 42;'))
bundle.addSource({
  content: new MagicString('console.log(answer);'),
  separator: '\n',
})

bundle.toString()
// var answer = 42;
// console.log(answer);
```

`bundle.append( str[, options ])` takes the same options object but reads only `separator`, which defaults to `''` rather than to the bundle separator:

```js
const bundle = new Bundle({ separator: '\n\n' })

bundle.addSource(new MagicString('a'))

bundle.append('b')
bundle.toString() // 'ab'

bundle.append('c', { separator: '\n' })
bundle.toString() // 'ab\nc'
```

### bundle.toMagicString()

Flattens the bundle into a single `MagicString`, so the concatenated result can be processed further with the full `MagicString` API:

```js
const bundle = new Bundle()
bundle.addSource(new MagicString('var answer = 42;'))
bundle.addSource(new MagicString('console.log(answer);'))

const s = bundle.toMagicString()
s.toString() // 'var answer = 42;\nconsole.log(answer);'

// now use any MagicString method on the combined result
s.prepend('(function () {\n').append('\n}());')
```

The returned string's `original` is the concatenation of every source's `original`, and all existing edits, inserts, intros, outros and separators are preserved, so `s.toString()` equals `bundle.toString()` and `s.generateMap()` maps back to that combined original. Because a `MagicString` maps to a single source, per-source `filename`s are not carried over - call `bundle.generateMap()` before flattening if you need the multi-source mapping.

## License

MIT

===== node_modules\why-is-node-running\README.md =====

# why-is-node-running

Node.js is running but you don't know why? `why-is-node-running` is here to help you.

## Installation

If you want to use `why-is-node-running` in your code, you can install it as a local dependency of your project. If you want to use it as a CLI, you can install it globally, or use `npx` to run it without installing it.

### As a local dependency

Node.js 20.11 and above (ECMAScript modules):

```bash
npm install --save-dev why-is-node-running
```

Node.js 8 or higher (CommonJS):

```bash
npm install --save-dev why-is-node-running@v2.x
```

### As a global package

```bash
npm install --global why-is-node-running
why-is-node-running /path/to/some/file.js
```

Alternatively if you do not want to install the package globally, you can run it with [`npx`](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/commands/npx):

```bash
npx why-is-node-running /path/to/some/file.js
```

## Usage (as a dependency)

```js
import whyIsNodeRunning from 'why-is-node-running' // should be your first import
import { createServer } from 'node:net'

function startServer () {
  const server = createServer()
  setInterval(() => {}, 1000)
  server.listen(0)
}

startServer()
startServer()

// logs out active handles that are keeping node running
setImmediate(() => whyIsNodeRunning())
```

Save the file as `example.js`, then execute:

```bash
node ./example.js
```

Here's the output:

```
There are 4 handle(s) keeping the process running

# Timeout
example.js:6  - setInterval(() => {}, 1000)
example.js:10 - startServer()

# TCPSERVERWRAP
example.js:7  - server.listen(0)
example.js:10 - startServer()

# Timeout
example.js:6  - setInterval(() => {}, 1000)
example.js:11 - startServer()

# TCPSERVERWRAP
example.js:7  - server.listen(0)
example.js:11 - startServer()
```

## Usage (as a CLI)

You can run `why-is-node-running` as a standalone if you don't want to include it inside your code. Sending `SIGUSR1`/`SIGINFO` signal to the process will produce the log. (`Ctrl + T` on macOS and BSD systems)

```bash
why-is-node-running /path/to/some/file.js
```

```
probing module /path/to/some/file.js
kill -SIGUSR1 31115 for logging
```

To trigger the log:

```
kill -SIGUSR1 31115
```

## Usage (with Node.js' `--import` option)

You can also use Node's [`--import`](https://nodejs.org/api/cli.html#--importmodule) option to preload `why-is-node-running`:

```bash
node --import why-is-node-running/include /path/to/some/file.js
```

The steps are otherwise the same as the above CLI section

## License

MIT


===== node_modules\xlsx\README.md =====

# [SheetJS](https://sheetjs.com)

The SheetJS Community Edition offers battle-tested open-source solutions for
extracting useful data from almost any complex spreadsheet and generating new
spreadsheets that will work with legacy and modern software alike.

[SheetJS Pro](https://sheetjs.com/pro) offers solutions beyond data processing:
Edit complex templates with ease; let out your inner Picasso with styling; make
custom sheets with images/graphs/PivotTables; evaluate formula expressions and
port calculations to web apps; automate common spreadsheet tasks, and much more!

## Documentation

- [API and Usage Documentation](https://docs.sheetjs.com)

- [Downloadable Scripts and Modules](https://cdn.sheetjs.com)

## Constellation

- <https://oss.sheetjs.com/notes/>: File Format Notes

- [`ssf`](packages/ssf): Format data using ECMA-376 spreadsheet format codes

- [`xlsx-cli`](packages/xlsx-cli): NodeJS command-line tool for processing files

- [`cfb`](https://git.sheetjs.com/SheetJS/js-cfb): Container (OLE/ZIP) file
processing library

- [`codepage`](https://git.sheetjs.com/SheetJS/js-codepage): Legacy text
encodings for XLS and other legacy spreadsheet formats

- [`dta`](packages/dta): Stata DTA file processor

- [`test_files`](https://github.com/sheetjs/test_files): Test files and various
plaintext baselines.

## License

Please consult the attached LICENSE file for details.  All rights not explicitly
granted by the Apache 2.0 License are reserved by the Original Author.



===== src\data\README.md =====

# Fuente bibliográfica de ECMC

`ecmc-orcid.json` procede exclusivamente del archivo `emcc_orcid.sql` proporcionado por el usuario. El volcado phpMyAdmin indica generación el 12 de octubre de 2026 a las 00:58:14 y contiene una sola tabla, `publicaciones`. No se ejecutó SQL: se extrajeron sus valores como datos.

La importación se limita a ECMC. Las demás escuelas conservan sus datos actuales. Los cuatro investigadores se identifican mediante el nombre y ORCID presentes en la fuente; no se les atribuyen correos, cargos, títulos académicos, fotos, biografías ni métricas externas que el archivo no proporciona.

## Recuentos y coautoría

- 140 filas originales y 135 trabajos bibliográficos únicos.
- 120 DOI distintos y 15 trabajos sin DOI.
- Cuatro DOI compartidos por varios investigadores generan cinco filas adicionales. Sus metadatos coinciden; se agrupan en un único trabajo y se conservan todas las asociaciones de investigadores y filas originales (`sourceRows`, posiciones desde 1 en el bloque `INSERT`).
- La suma institucional, sin contar repetidamente los trabajos compartidos, es de 1.388 citas conocidas. Las 140 filas originales suman 1.409 citas por repetir coautorías.
- Juan Astudillo León (`0000-0002-7291-3584`): 43 asociaciones, 296 citas conocidas.
- Manuel Eugenio Morocho-Cayamcela (`0000-0002-4705-7923`): 47 asociaciones, 955 citas conocidas.
- Rigoberto Fonseca-Delgado (`0000-0002-8890-3911`): 19 asociaciones, 130 citas conocidas.
- Jefferson Alexander Moreno-Guaicha (`0000-0002-0380-4739`): 31 asociaciones, 28 citas conocidas.

El campo `Investigador` indica una asociación bibliográfica con un ORCID, no la lista completa ni el orden de autores de cada publicación. `authors` y `authorIds` contienen solo estos investigadores vinculados. No se inventa un autor principal ni un propietario: `ownerId` usa el identificador técnico `ecmc-orcid-import`.

## Fidelidad y datos ausentes

- Se preservan los nueve tipos originales en `bibliographicSource.publicationType`: 63 artículos de revista, 33 capítulos, 29 artículos de congreso, una tesis, tres conjuntos de datos, un trabajo de tipo `other`, un software, dos libros editados y dos números de revista. Se presentan en el catálogo bibliográfico como `publicacion`; no se fabrican proyectos.
- Los años abarcan 2011–2027. Los dos capítulos de 2027 figuran así en el archivo y se conservan sin adelantar ni corregir su fecha.
- No hay fechas exactas de publicación ni semestres, líneas de investigación, resúmenes, proyectos o constancia de revisión institucional. Se dejan ausentes o vacíos según el contrato de datos. `createdAt` y `updatedAt` registran la ingesta, no la fecha de publicación.
- Hay 19 trabajos con citas `NULL`, dos medios de publicación vacíos, 15 DOI ausentes y 66 filas originales con SJR desconocido. Las citas desconocidas permanecen como `null` en `bibliographicSource.citations`; el campo numérico existente usa cero únicamente como valor neutro para agregación, sin convertir el dato desconocido en una medición de cero citas.
- Los valores SJR `Sin dato` y `-` se normalizan a `null`. Los cuartiles y puntuaciones existentes se mantienen sin estimaciones.
- Se decodifica `&amp;` a `&` (siete filas originales) y se convierte el espacio no separable a espacio normal (13 filas), sin modificar el contenido bibliográfico restante.
- Los identificadores de producto son estables: prefijo `ecmc-orcid-` más los primeros 24 caracteres hexadecimales de SHA-256 de `doi:{DOI normalizado}` o, cuando falta DOI, de `title:{año}:{título normalizado}`. Los identificadores de investigador se basan en su ORCID.

## Clasificación temática temporal

El SQL no relaciona publicaciones con líneas de investigación. Para hacer útil el contenido provisional se aplica un diccionario transparente en `src/services/ecmcResearchLineDictionary.ts`, solo a las 135 publicaciones de este archivo y solo a partir de sus títulos. Reconoce términos en inglés y español, compara puntajes entre las seis líneas oficiales de ECMC y deja sin asignar los casos con poca evidencia o empate. Cada sugerencia guarda la versión del diccionario, los términos coincidentes y la solidez relativa; esto no es una probabilidad ni una clasificación provista por ORCID. La interfaz y las exportaciones la identifican como temporal. Los perfiles de investigadores, otras escuelas y registros futuros no se clasifican con este diccionario.

El estado técnico `verificado` se utiliza únicamente para permitir la visibilidad pública del conjunto importado en el contrato actual del portal. `bibliographicSource` identifica la procedencia, la interfaz lo distingue como «Importado ORCID» y no existe `verifiedAt` ni una aprobación atribuida al comité.

## Almacenamiento local

La migración reconoce los antiguos productos sintéticos de ECMC `prod-001` a `prod-015` y docentes `doc-001` a `doc-006`. Estos identificadores están separados de los nuevos registros importados; no representan los identificadores de investigadores reales. Las credenciales de demostración se mantienen separadas de estos perfiles bibliográficos.


===== test-assets\mobile\footer-polish\README.md =====

# Footer móvil: tipografía y espacio inferior

Rama: `mobile-polish`. Sin merge a `main`.

Causa: `.institutional-landing-footer-group h2` forzaba `Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif` en `src/index.css`.

El ajuste se limita al footer con ancho inferior a 760 px. Sus encabezados heredan la misma familia del cuerpo, con peso 600 y tamaño 1.1rem. Se mantiene el resto de sus colores, márgenes y contenido. Se añade `padding-bottom: calc(24px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))`, enlaces de al menos 44 px de alto, separación vertical de 12 px y logo al 85 % de su ancho anterior.

## Verificación en Chromium / Edge

Móvil: 390×844, emulación móvil y táctil, escala 3. Acceso al footer mediante gestos CDP desde YTLC.

| Comprobación | Resultado |
| --- | --- |
| Los tres encabezados coinciden con `getComputedStyle(document.body).fontFamily` | Pasa |
| Resto de textos del footer con la misma familia sans | Pasa |
| Encabezados con peso 600 y tamaño 17.6 px | Pasa |
| Enlaces: altura mínima / separación vertical | 44 px / 12 px |
| Logo: ancho antes → después | 190 → 161.5 px (85 %) |
| Padding inferior en emulación sin área segura adicional | 24 px |
| Última línea completamente visible tras el desplazamiento táctil | Pasa; borde inferior a 822.81 px de 844 px |
| Desbordamiento horizontal | Ninguno |
| CLS móvil antes → después | 0 → 0 |
| Comprobación adicional a 360×740 | Fuente correcta, enlaces ≥ 44 px, última línea visible, CLS 0 y sin desbordamiento |
| Footer escritorio 1366 px: diferencia de píxeles antes/después | 0 |
| Footer en el límite de 760 px: diferencia de píxeles | 0 |
| Chequeo de tipos y build | Sin errores |

La familia calculada del cuerpo y del footer es `system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif`.

`390-before.png` y `390-after.png` muestran el footer completo. Las capturas `390-*-bottom.png` muestran la última línea en el viewport después de gestos táctiles. `desktop-*.png` y `760-*.png` contienen las comparaciones fuera del alcance móvil.

Detalle de medición: el anclaje existente deja el desplazamiento móvil en 6700 px frente a un máximo geométrico de 6716 px; la última línea permanece completamente visible. No se modificó ese comportamiento. A 760 px se registra CLS previo de aproximadamente 0.0944 y posterior de 0.0947, originado en la bienvenida y sus logos, fuera del footer; sus fuentes están identificadas en `verification.json`. El footer de 760 px es pixel-idéntico y no recibe las reglas nuevas.

El servidor de desarrollo registró `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` antes y después del ajuste. El chequeo de tipos y el build terminaron correctamente; no se modificaron observadores ni transiciones.

===== src\types\index.ts =====

/**
 * Tipos de datos centrales de SIMAPC - Universidad Yachay Tech
 * Conforme al Documento de Requisitos e Historias de Usuario (HU01 - HU11)
 */

export type ProductType = 'publicacion' | 'proyecto';

export type ProductStatus = 'cargado' | 'verificado' | 'rechazado';

export type ProjectStatus = 'activo' | 'en_pausa' | 'finalizado' | 'cancelado';

export interface ProductAttachment {
  id: string;
  fileName: string;
  mimeType: 'application/pdf';
  size?: number;
  isSynthetic?: boolean;
}

export interface ProjectProgressReport {
  id: string;
  periodStart: string;
  periodEnd: string;
  progressPercent: number;
  summary: string;
  completedActivities: string[];
  achievedProducts: string[];
  blockers?: string;
  nextSteps: string;
  statusAfterReport: Extract<ProjectStatus, 'activo' | 'en_pausa'>;
  reportedAt: string;
  isSynthetic?: boolean;
}

export interface ProjectClosureReport {
  id: string;
  closedAt: string;
  finalStatus: Extract<ProjectStatus, 'finalizado' | 'cancelado'>;
  summary: string;
  deliveredProducts: string[];
  pendingItems: string[];
  lessonsLearned?: string;
  isSynthetic?: boolean;
}

export type AcademicSemester =
  | '2021-1' | '2021-2'
  | '2022-1' | '2022-2'
  | '2023-1' | '2023-2'
  | '2024-1' | '2024-2'
  | '2025-1' | '2025-2'
  | '2026-1' | '2026-2';

export type { OfficialResearchLine, SchoolCode } from '../constants/schools';
import type { OfficialResearchLine } from '../constants/schools';

export type TeacherResearchSublines = Partial<Record<OfficialResearchLine, string[]>>;
export type SyntheticAcademicProfileField = 'orcid' | 'githubUrl' | 'googleScholarId' | 'scopusAuthorId' | 'webOfScienceId';
export type SyntheticBibliometricField = 'googleScholarHIndex' | 'scopusHIndex';

export type AcademicDegree = 'PhD' | 'MSc' | 'BSc' | 'Other';

export const PRODUCT_STATUS_LABELS: Record<ProductStatus, string> = {
  cargado: 'Pendiente de verificación',
  verificado: 'Verificado',
  rechazado: 'Producto en observación',
};

export const PROJECT_STATUS_LABELS: Record<ProjectStatus, string> = {
  activo: 'Activo',
  en_pausa: 'En pausa',
  finalizado: 'Finalizado',
  cancelado: 'Cancelado',
};

export interface ScientificProduct {
  id: string; // ej. prod-001
  type: ProductType;
  title: string;
  authors: string[];
  ownerId: string; // ID del profesor registrado propietario
  school: string; // Por defecto 'ECMC' (escalable para futuras escuelas)
  year: number;
  semester?: AcademicSemester; // Compatibilidad con productos existentes y serie histórica
  publicationDate?: string; // Fecha ISO para publicaciones
  projectStartDate?: string;
  projectEndDate?: string;
  researchLine: OfficialResearchLine | ''; // Official or temporary dictionary classification; empty when no line is suggested.
  abstract: string;
  status: ProductStatus;
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
  verifiedAt?: string;
  rejectionReason?: string;
  citations: number; // 0 o número de citas (fuente identificada como simulada en demo)
  authorIds?: string[]; // Researchers explicitly associated with this work by the imported source.
  bibliographicSource?: {
    dataset: string;
    publicationType: string;
    researcherOrcids: string[];
    sourceRows: number[];
    citations: number | null;
    sjrQuartile: string | null;
    sjrScore: number | null;
    researchLineClassification?: {
      method: 'temporary-keyword-dictionary';
      version: string;
      strength: 'media' | 'alta';
      matchedKeywords: string[];
    };
  };

  // Específico para publicaciones
  doi?: string;
  venue?: string; // Revista, conferencia, medio
  volumeIssue?: string;
  articleAttachment?: ProductAttachment;
  privacyConsentAt?: string;

  // Específico para proyectos de investigación
  projectCode?: string; // ej. ECMC-INV-2024-008
  projectDirector?: string;
  fundingVenue?: string;
  projectStatus?: ProjectStatus;
  projectParticipants?: string[];
  projectDurationMonths?: number;
  expectedProducts?: string[];
  projectProgressReports?: ProjectProgressReport[];
  projectClosureReport?: ProjectClosureReport;
}

export interface TeacherUser {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  email: string; // Debe pertenecer al dominio @yachaytech.edu.ec
  rank: string; // Cargo institucional
  academicDegree?: AcademicDegree;
  academicField?: string;
  yachayEntryYear?: number;
  profileImage?: string; // Imagen optimizada en formato data URL
  researchLines?: OfficialResearchLine[];
  researchSublines?: TeacherResearchSublines;
  researchLine?: OfficialResearchLine; // Compatibilidad con perfiles guardados antes de la selección múltiple
  orcid?: string; // Formato 0000-000X-XXXX-XXXX
  githubUrl?: string;
  googleScholarId?: string;
  googleScholarHIndex?: number;
  scopusAuthorId?: string;
  scopusHIndex?: number;
  webOfScienceId?: string;
  syntheticAcademicProfileFields?: SyntheticAcademicProfileField[];
  syntheticBibliometricFields?: SyntheticBibliometricField[];
  syntheticProfileSeedVersion?: number;
  bio?: string;
  school: string;
  role: 'teacher' | 'student' | 'reviewer_demo' | 'developer'; // Perfiles de acceso del portal
  createdAt: string;
}

export interface UserNotification {
  id: string;
  userId: string;
  productId: string;
  productTitle: string;
  status: ProductStatus;
  reason?: string;
  message: string;
  read: boolean;
  createdAt: string;
}

export interface TeacherMetrics {
  teacher: TeacherUser;
  publicationsCount: number;
  projectsCount: number;
  citationsTotal: number;
}

export interface SchoolMetrics {
  totalPublications: number;
  totalProjects: number;
  totalCitations: number;
  researchLinesWithProduction: number;
}

export interface AgileHU {
  rf: string;
  epic: string;
  hu: string;
  title: string;
  actor: string;
  description: string;
  priority: 'Must' | 'Should' | 'Could';
  storyPoints: number;
  status: 'Verificado con evidencia' | 'Implementado sin verificar' | 'Pendiente' | 'Bloqueado';
  relatedRnfs: string[];
  acceptanceCriteria: {
    id: string;
    description: string;
  }[];
  tasks: {
    id: string;
    description: string;
    type: 'UX/UI' | 'Validación' | 'Backend/API' | 'Base de datos' | 'Seguridad' | 'Integración' | 'Pruebas' | 'Análisis' | 'Regla de negocio' | 'Arquitectura' | 'Diseño técnico';
    relatedCA: string;
    completed: boolean;
  }[];
  testCases: {
    id: string;
    type: 'Aceptación' | 'Seguridad' | 'Funcional' | 'Integración' | 'Resiliencia' | 'Rendimiento' | 'Validación' | 'Regla de negocio';
    relatedCA: string;
    summary: string;
    expectedResult: string;
    passed: boolean;
    evidenceText: string;
  }[];
}

export interface FilterState {
  searchQuery: string;
  productType: 'todos' | ProductType;
  teacherId: 'todos' | string;
  periodYear: 'todos' | string;
  researchLine: 'todas' | OfficialResearchLine;
  status: 'todos' | ProductStatus;
}


===== src\constants\demoAccounts.ts =====

import { TeacherUser } from '../types';
import { SCHOOLS, type SchoolConfig } from './schools';

// Default to the current public demo; production builds can explicitly disable it.
export const DEMO_ENABLED = import.meta.env.DEV || (import.meta.env.VITE_ENABLE_DEMO ?? 'true') === 'true';

// Public test fixtures for this local prototype, not production credentials.
interface DemoAccount {
  user: TeacherUser;
  password: string;
  credentialId: string;
  aliases?: readonly string[];
}

function accountsForSchool(school: SchoolConfig): DemoAccount[] {
  const suffix = school.code.toLowerCase();
  const teacher: TeacherUser = {id:school.code === 'ECMC' ? 'doc-001' : `demo-teacher-${suffix}`, name:'Profesor de prueba', email:'profesor@yachaytech.edu.ec', role:'teacher', rank:'Profesor', school:school.code, researchLines:[], createdAt:'2026-10-13'};
  return [
    {user:teacher, password:'Profesor2026!', credentialId:'doc-001'},
    {user:{id:`demo-student-${suffix}`, name:'Estudiante de prueba', email:'estudiante@yachaytech.edu.ec', role:'student', rank:'Estudiante colaborador', school:school.code, bio:`Estudiante colaborador de ${school.name}.`, createdAt:'2026-10-10'}, password:'Estudiante2026!', credentialId:'demo-student-ecmc', aliases:['estudiante.ecmc@yachaytech.edu.ec']},
    {user:{id:school.code === 'ECMC' ? 'demo-reviewer' : `demo-reviewer-${suffix}`, name:'Comité Científico', email:'comite@yachaytech.edu.ec', role:'reviewer_demo', rank:'Miembro del Comité', school:school.code, createdAt:'2026-09-30'}, password:'Comite2026!', credentialId:'demo-reviewer'},
  ];
}

// Shared credentials select a stable identity per school. Keep the existing ECMC
// IDs so saved products, role assignments and student collaborations still work.
const orderedSchools = [...SCHOOLS.filter(school => school.code === 'ECMC'), ...SCHOOLS.filter(school => school.code !== 'ECMC')];
const demoAccounts: DemoAccount[] = [
  ...orderedSchools.flatMap(accountsForSchool),
  {user:{id:'demo-developer', name:'Equipo de desarrollo', email:'desarrollo@yachaytech.edu.ec', role:'developer', rank:'Desarrollador', school:'ECMC', createdAt:'2026-09-30'}, password:'Equipo2026!', credentialId:'demo-developer'},
];

export const DEMO_ACCOUNTS = DEMO_ENABLED ? demoAccounts : [];

// Keep recognizing persisted demo identities even when their login is disabled.
export function isDemoAccount(identity: {id?: string; email?: string}): boolean {
  const email = identity.email?.trim().toLowerCase();
  return demoAccounts.some(({user, aliases}) => user.id === identity.id || user.email === email || aliases?.includes(email || ''));
}

export const canReview = (user: TeacherUser | null) => user?.role === 'developer' || user?.role === 'reviewer_demo';
export const canDevelop = (user: TeacherUser | null) => user?.role === 'developer';


===== src\constants\ecmcOrcidData.ts =====

import sourcePublications from '../data/ecmc-orcid.json';
import type { ScientificProduct, TeacherUser } from '../types';
import { ECMC_RESEARCH_DICTIONARY_VERSION, suggestEcmcResearchLine } from '../services/ecmcResearchLineDictionary';

export const ECMC_ORCID_DATASET = 'emcc_orcid.sql';
// Ingestion time; this is not a publication date or an institutional review date.
export const ECMC_ORCID_IMPORTED_AT = '2026-10-13T22:52:12Z';

const researcherId = (orcid: string) => `ecmc-orcid-researcher-${orcid}`;
const researchers = new Map<string, { name: string; orcid: string }>();
for (const publication of sourcePublications) {
  for (const researcher of publication.researchers) {
    researchers.set(researcher.orcid, researcher);
  }
}

// Only the names and ORCID identifiers explicitly present in the supplied source.
// Empty required fields do not assert an email, institutional rank or degree.
export const INITIAL_TEACHERS: TeacherUser[] = [...researchers.values()].map(researcher => ({
  id: researcherId(researcher.orcid),
  name: researcher.name,
  orcid: researcher.orcid,
  email: '',
  rank: '',
  researchLines: [],
  school: 'ECMC',
  role: 'teacher',
  createdAt: ECMC_ORCID_IMPORTED_AT,
}));

export const INITIAL_PRODUCTS: ScientificProduct[] = sourcePublications.map(publication => {
  const lineSuggestion = suggestEcmcResearchLine(publication.title);
  return {
    id: publication.id,
    type: 'publicacion',
    title: publication.title,
    authors: publication.researchers.map(researcher => researcher.name),
    authorIds: publication.researchers.map(researcher => researcherId(researcher.orcid)),
    // An ORCID association does not identify an owner or the publication's first author.
    ownerId: 'ecmc-orcid-import',
    school: 'ECMC',
    year: publication.year,
    researchLine: lineSuggestion?.line || '',
    abstract: '',
    // Public import visibility only. The UI identifies these as imported ORCID
    // records, not an approval by the scientific committee; verifiedAt stays absent.
    status: 'verificado',
    citations: publication.citations ?? 0,
    doi: publication.doi || undefined,
    venue: publication.venue || undefined,
    createdAt: ECMC_ORCID_IMPORTED_AT,
    updatedAt: ECMC_ORCID_IMPORTED_AT,
    bibliographicSource: {
      dataset: ECMC_ORCID_DATASET,
      publicationType: publication.publicationType,
      researcherOrcids: publication.researchers.map(researcher => researcher.orcid),
      sourceRows: publication.sourceRows,
      citations: publication.citations,
      sjrQuartile: publication.sjrQuartile,
      sjrScore: publication.sjrScore,
      researchLineClassification: lineSuggestion ? {
        method: 'temporary-keyword-dictionary',
        version: ECMC_RESEARCH_DICTIONARY_VERSION,
        strength: lineSuggestion.strength,
        matchedKeywords: lineSuggestion.matchedKeywords,
      } : undefined,
    },
  };
});

===== src\constants\researchStageSlides.ts =====

import { SCHOOLS, type OfficialResearchLine, type SchoolCode } from './schools';

export interface ResearchStageSlide {
  readonly title: string;
  readonly line: OfficialResearchLine;
  readonly accentWords: readonly number[];
}

/** One existing SVG motif accompanies each school presentation. */
const SCHOOL_STAGE_MOTIFS: Record<SchoolCode, OfficialResearchLine> = {
  ECIAA: 'Ciencias Agrícolas',
  ECBI: 'Biología celular, biología molecular y genética',
  ECFN: 'Materiales nanoestructurados, síntesis y caracterización',
  ECTEA: 'Geomática aplicada a las geociencias',
  ECMC: 'Inteligencia artificial',
  ECQI: 'Química medicinal y farmacología molecular',
  YTLC: 'Sociolinguistics/Language and Culture',
};

/** School names share the official configuration; each school has exactly one slide. */
export const RESEARCH_STAGE_SLIDES = SCHOOLS.reduce((slides, school) => {
  slides[school.code] = [{
    title: school.name,
    line: SCHOOL_STAGE_MOTIFS[school.code],
    accentWords: school.name.split(' ').flatMap((_, index) =>
      index >= (school.code === 'YTLC' ? 0 : 3) ? [index] : [],
    ),
  }];
  return slides;
}, {} as Record<SchoolCode, readonly [ResearchStageSlide]>);

const SCHOOL_VENUES: Record<AdditionalSchoolCode, string> = {
  ECIAA: 'Revista Andina de Sistemas Agroalimentarios',
  ECBI: 'Revista de Biodiversidad y Ciencias Biológicas',
  ECFN: 'Journal of Applied Physics and Materials',
  ECTEA: 'Revista de Geociencias y Ambiente Andino',
  ECQI: 'Journal of Chemistry and Sustainable Engineering',
  YTLC: 'Journal of Language Education and Technology',
};

const schoolConfigs = SCHOOLS.filter((school) => school.code !== 'ECMC');

export const INITIAL_SCHOOL_TEACHERS: TeacherUser[] = schoolConfigs.flatMap((school) => {
  const schoolCode = school.code as AdditionalSchoolCode;
  return TEACHERS_BY_SCHOOL[schoolCode].map((seed, teacherIndex) => {
    const researchLines = school.researchLines.filter((_, lineIndex) => lineIndex % 2 === teacherIndex) as OfficialResearchLine[];
    const researchSublines = Object.fromEntries(researchLines.map((line) => [line, SUBLINES_BY_RESEARCH_LINE[line] || []]));
    const teacherNumber = String(teacherIndex + 1).padStart(2, '0');
    return {
      id: `seed-${schoolCode.toLowerCase()}-teacher-${teacherNumber}`,
      name: seed.name,
      email: `investigador.${schoolCode.toLowerCase()}.${teacherNumber}@yachaytech.edu.ec`,
      rank: seed.rank,
      academicDegree: seed.academicDegree,
      academicField: seed.academicField,
      yachayEntryYear: seed.yachayEntryYear,
      researchLines,
      researchSublines,
      orcid: `0000-0002-${String(4100 + schoolConfigs.indexOf(school) * 20 + teacherIndex).padStart(4, '0')}-${String(1200 + schoolConfigs.indexOf(school) * 10 + teacherIndex).padStart(4, '0')}`,
      githubUrl: `https://github.com/${seed.githubSlug}`,
      googleScholarId: seed.scholarId,
      googleScholarHIndex: seed.scholarHIndex,
      scopusAuthorId: seed.scopusId,
      scopusHIndex: seed.scopusHIndex,
      webOfScienceId: seed.webOfScienceId,
      syntheticAcademicProfileFields: ['orcid', 'githubUrl', 'googleScholarId', 'scopusAuthorId', 'webOfScienceId'],
      syntheticBibliometricFields: ['googleScholarHIndex', 'scopusHIndex'],
      bio: seed.bio,
      school: schoolCode,
      role: 'teacher',
      createdAt: `${seed.yachayEntryYear}-08-01T08:00:00Z`,
    };
  });
});

const teacherById = new Map(INITIAL_SCHOOL_TEACHERS.map((teacher) => [teacher.id, teacher]));
const projectStates = ['en_pausa', 'finalizado', 'cancelado', 'en_pausa', 'finalizado', 'cancelado'] as const;

const schoolPublications: ScientificProduct[] = schoolConfigs.flatMap((school, schoolIndex) => {
  const schoolCode = school.code as AdditionalSchoolCode;
  return school.researchLines.map((researchLine, lineIndex) => {
    const teacherIndex = lineIndex % 2;
    const ownerId = `seed-${schoolCode.toLowerCase()}-teacher-${String(teacherIndex + 1).padStart(2, '0')}`;
    const owner = teacherById.get(ownerId)!;
    const coauthor = teacherById.get(`seed-${schoolCode.toLowerCase()}-teacher-${String(2 - teacherIndex).padStart(2, '0')}`)!;
    const detail = PUBLICATION_DETAILS[researchLine] || {
      title: `Avances de investigación en ${researchLine}`,
      abstract: `Estudio interdisciplinario sobre ${researchLine.toLowerCase()} y sus aplicaciones en contextos regionales.`,
    };
    const year = 2022 + ((schoolIndex + lineIndex) % 5);
    const month = ((schoolIndex * 2 + lineIndex) % 12) + 1;
    const day = ((schoolIndex + lineIndex * 3) % 27) + 1;
    const date = `${year}-${String(month).padStart(2, '0')}-${String(day).padStart(2, '0')}`;
    return {
      id: `seed-${schoolCode.toLowerCase()}-publication-${String(lineIndex + 1).padStart(2, '0')}`,
      type: 'publicacion',
      title: detail.title,
      authors: [owner.name, coauthor.name],
      ownerId,
      school: schoolCode,
      year,
      publicationDate: date,
      researchLine,
      abstract: detail.abstract,
      status: 'verificado',
      venue: SCHOOL_VENUES[schoolCode],
      volumeIssue: `Vol. ${year - 2020}, núm. ${((lineIndex + schoolIndex) % 3) + 1}`,
      citations: 3 + ((schoolIndex * 5 + lineIndex * 7) % 24),
      createdAt: `${date}T09:00:00Z`,
      updatedAt: `${date}T09:00:00Z`,
      verifiedAt: `${date}T09:00:00Z`,
    };
  });
});

const schoolProjects: ScientificProduct[] = schoolConfigs.flatMap((school, schoolIndex) => {
  const schoolCode = school.code as AdditionalSchoolCode;
  return PROJECT_DETAILS[schoolCode].map((project, projectIndex) => {
    const projectLineIndex = projectIndex === 0 ? 0 : school.researchLines.length - 1;
    const teacherIndex = projectLineIndex % 2;
    const ownerId = `seed-${schoolCode.toLowerCase()}-teacher-${String(teacherIndex + 1).padStart(2, '0')}`;
    const owner = teacherById.get(ownerId)!;
    const collaborator = teacherById.get(`seed-${schoolCode.toLowerCase()}-teacher-${String(2 - teacherIndex).padStart(2, '0')}`)!;
    const researchLine = school.researchLines[projectLineIndex] as OfficialResearchLine;
    const state = projectIndex === 0 ? 'activo' : projectStates[schoolIndex];
    const startYear = projectIndex === 0 ? 2025 : 2023 + (schoolIndex % 3);
    const startDate = `${startYear}-02-01`;
    const endDate = state === 'finalizado' || state === 'cancelado' ? `${startYear + 1}-12-15` : `${startYear + 2}-11-30`;
    const projectNumber = projectIndex + 1;
    const expectedProducts = projectIndex === 0
      ? ['Protocolo de trabajo documentado', 'Base de resultados compartida', 'Informe de avance del proyecto']
      : ['Conjunto de datos organizado', 'Artículo de resultados', 'Material de divulgación académica'];
    const progress = {
      id: `seed-${schoolCode.toLowerCase()}-project-${projectNumber}-progress`,
      periodStart: startDate,
      periodEnd: `${startYear + 1}-01-31`,
      progressPercent: state === 'finalizado' || state === 'cancelado' ? 100 : 48 + schoolIndex * 4,
      summary: 'El equipo completó la planificación, organizó las fuentes de información y avanzó en el análisis de resultados.',
      completedActivities: ['Plan de trabajo acordado', 'Revisión de fuentes y antecedentes', 'Primer ciclo de análisis'],
      achievedProducts: ['Protocolo de investigación', 'Matriz de datos inicial'],
      nextSteps: 'Completar el siguiente ciclo de trabajo y preparar los productos previstos.',
      statusAfterReport: state === 'en_pausa' ? 'en_pausa' as const : 'activo' as const,
      reportedAt: `${startYear + 1}-02-10T12:00:00Z`,
    };
    const isClosed = state === 'finalizado' || state === 'cancelado';
    return {
      id: `seed-${schoolCode.toLowerCase()}-project-${String(projectNumber).padStart(2, '0')}`,
      type: 'proyecto',
      title: project.title,
      authors: [owner.name, collaborator.name],
      ownerId,
      projectDirector: owner.name,
      projectCode: `${schoolCode}-INV-${startYear}-${String(projectNumber).padStart(3, '0')}`,
      school: schoolCode,
      year: startYear,
      projectStartDate: startDate,
      projectEndDate: endDate,
      researchLine,
      abstract: project.abstract,
      status: 'verificado',
      projectStatus: state,
      projectParticipants: [owner.name, collaborator.name],
      projectDurationMonths: isClosed ? 22 : 30,
      expectedProducts,
      projectProgressReports: isClosed ? [] : [progress],
      projectClosureReport: isClosed ? {
        id: `seed-${schoolCode.toLowerCase()}-project-${projectNumber}-closure`,
        closedAt: endDate,
        finalStatus: state as 'finalizado' | 'cancelado',
        summary: state === 'finalizado' ? 'El equipo completó las actividades y entregó los productos principales del proyecto.' : 'El equipo documentó los avances y cerró formalmente el proyecto de acuerdo con su planificación.',
        deliveredProducts: expectedProducts.slice(0, 2),
        pendingItems: [],
        lessonsLearned: 'La coordinación interdisciplinaria permitió organizar las tareas y compartir los resultados con la comunidad académica.',
      } : undefined,
      fundingVenue: 'Fondo institucional de investigación',
      citations: 0,
      createdAt: `${startDate}T09:00:00Z`,
      updatedAt: `${startDate}T09:00:00Z`,
      verifiedAt: `${startDate}T09:00:00Z`,
    };
  });
});

export const INITIAL_SCHOOL_PRODUCTS: ScientificProduct[] = [...schoolPublications, ...schoolProjects];


===== src\constants\seedData.ts =====

import type { UserNotification } from '../types';

export { INITIAL_TEACHERS, INITIAL_PRODUCTS } from './ecmcOrcidData';

// Remove only these old ECMC fixtures during the one-time local migration.
// User-created records and the six other schools are not demo fixtures here.
export const LEGACY_ECMC_PRODUCT_IDS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(
  Array.from({ length: 15 }, (_, index) => `prod-${String(index + 1).padStart(3, '0')}`)
);
export const LEGACY_ECMC_TEACHER_IDS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(
  Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, index) => `doc-${String(index + 1).padStart(3, '0')}`)
);

export const INITIAL_NOTIFICATIONS: UserNotification[] = [];
